title: Planning a Lesson Around the Pupil
whatItIs: Lesson planning is one of the 3 areas marked on the ADI part 3 test and the standards check. Its 4 competences cover goals, structure, practice area and adapting the plan.
keyFacts: Identify goals and needs: ask suitable questions, listen actively and notice body language.
Needs change during the lesson, so this can't be 'ticked off' at the start and forgotten.
Not taught this pupil before? An assessment drive before finalising the plan is fine.
Part 3 and standards check: discuss goals and risk management at the start, in no more than 3 minutes.
Stretch the pupil without overwhelming them; don't keep them to very quiet junctions without a risk reason.

rows: Pupil says what they want; understanding checked
Plan agreed and based on the pupil's goals
Realistic challenge, focused on the plan
Responds to performance and to concerns

a.label: Reasons to adapt the plan
points: Pupil out of their depth or uncomfortable
Pupil already competent at the task

b.label: Wrong ways to change it
points: Changing the plan without a reason
Not explaining the change to the pupil

onTheTest.question: A pupil is nervous about entering roundabouts. Which practice area best fits DVSA guidance?
options: Roundabouts that stretch but don't overwhelm them
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.24: stretch the pupil without overwhelming them. Not a fast multi-lane roundabout first, but not only very quiet junctions either.

onTheTest.question: You haven't taught a pupil before. What can you do before finalising the lesson plan?
options: Ask them to do an assessment drive
Use your standard lesson for their hours
Ask the examiner what to teach
Spend the lesson on one manoeuvre
onTheTest.why: Examiner guidance 3.10: with little or no experience of the pupil, suggest an assessment drive, leaving time for development and feedback.

traps: A pupil doing well is also a reason to rethink the plan, not only a pupil who struggles.
Marking 'goals' 0 but 'structure' 2 or 3 is inconsistent: with no goals, no structure can be agreed.
Pupils whose needs exceed your competence should be transferred to an appropriate colleague.
